Modelled figures have a ±15% margin of error. Every figure you share replaces an estimate with a real number.
How lists and filters are ordered

One rule on every screen: filters go from broadest to narrowest (discipline → track → title → location), then sorting. “For you” in Jobs starts sorted by match score, then newest, with every other sort available; the other lists default to newest. Companies: reports → median as the tie-breaker, with unknown founding years at the end. Post replies: the accepted answer first, then the most “Helpful”, then the oldest.

Happens off the platform: every ad carries the company’s email or phone, and the engineer sends a CV from their personal email or calls. No forms, no tracking, no middleman. The “CV reviewer” tool runs on your device and doesn’t upload the file.
The expected range on job ads

Companies don’t write a number. Range = lower to upper quartile of the market for (discipline × years of experience) × city factor × sub-discipline factor × exact-title factor (fresh graduate 0.90 → director 1.45) × employer-type factor (government 0.72 → back office 1.90). The midpoint is shown with the number of reports and the quality badge.

Discipline 40 points · sub-discipline 25 (neighbouring tracks 12) · years of experience 20 (±2 years 10) · location 10 (same region 5) · title 5. 85 and above is an “exact match” and triggers an instant notification; 65–84 is “strong” and shows under “For you” without a notification.
